LBY.note: Says nothing on a public digital-skills programme or a measured share.
Mentions power cuts only as a story, with no outage count for the grid.
Says the incubator assists displaced people but states no registration or digital access.

systems.owner: European Union, co-implemented by SPARK and Super Novae

LBY.note: The programme is EU-funded, not a Libyan state law or fund.

facts.fact: SPARK states that Silphium Labs, a business incubator founded with Omar Al-Mokhtar University and ION+ under the EU-funded Libya Startup Programme, took in Smart Tech in 2024 and ran a final pitching event in May 2025 awarding 15,000 euro seed funding.
